classification.difficultyReason: Transfer the given within-triangle side ratio to the larger triangle to infer its base, subtract the extra segment to recover the original base, then determine the directed scale factor.

content.prompt:
Determine the scale factor for these similar triangles if $AB$ is half the length of $BC$.
Let $\triangle ABC$ be the original triangle.

spec.description: Nested right triangles share C. C, B and Q are collinear, and C, A and P are collinear. AB and PQ are perpendicular to the base. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black in house style.
spec.mathematics: AB:BC = 1:2; PQ = 5 cm; BQ = 4 cm. Coordinates preserve the given ratio and similarity without printing inferred lengths.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and vertex labels are visible.

answer.worked:
Corresponding sides have the same ratio, so $PQ:CQ=AB:BC=1:2$.
$$\begin{aligned}CQ&=2\times5=10\text{ cm}\\BC&=10-4=6\text{ cm}\\AB&=\frac12\times6=3\text{ cm}\\\text{Scale factor}&=\frac{PQ}{AB}=\frac53.\end{aligned}$$
